title: EntangledEdge: A Distributed System for Orbital Quantum Sensing and Learning
authors: Mohammad Abrarul Hasanat, Amit Samanta, Jason Ludmir, Tirthak Patel, Rohan Basu Roy
abstract: An orbital quantum sensor is more precise than classical and holds its information in a quantum state's superposition and entanglement, which classical measurement collapses. Learning on quantum-sensed data therefore requires a distributed system in which the data stay quantum from sensor to inference. We present EntangledEdge, the first system architecture to unify orbital quantum sensing and learning end-to-end, with a quantum data plane and a classical control plane. It routes each event to a channel-matched model in a capacity-diverse bank, adapts its detection threshold without labels, and aggregates across stations by hardware fidelity. Evaluated with a hybrid prototype (real quantum processors, simulated orbit-to-ground link) over satellite telemetry, EntangledEdge achieves high-quality inference at bounded per-event cost, improves quantum processor utilization, and scales with fleet size.
summary: This paper introduces EntangledEdge, a novel distributed system designed to perform quantum sensing and machine learning end-to-end across space and ground stations. It solves the critical problem of preserving quantum information during transmission by using quantum teleportation. The architecture achieves high-quality inference while managing real-world constraints like decoherence and data sparsity.
main_problem: Developing a distributed system for quantum sensing data that remains quantum from the sensor in orbit to the inference engine on the ground, circumventing classical measurement collapse.
main_result: The proposed EntangledEdge architecture achieves high-quality inference by unifying sensing and learning end-to-end, showing superior performance over classical and centralized methods.
method: The system uses quantum teleportation to transfer the sensed quantum state from the satellite to the ground QPU, followed by quantum autoencoder learning.
model_or_system: The system involves an orbital quantum sensor interacting with a field, transmitting the state via a quantum link (teleportation) to a ground QPU for processing. It utilizes a quantum data plane and a classical control plane.
key_observables: F1 Score, detection quality, latency, throughput, and QPU utilization.
important_parameters: Quantum state superposition and entanglement, hardware fidelity, and the short coherence times ($T_2$) of the qubits.
main_assumptions: Quantum data cannot be buffered or copied on the satellite due to the no-cloning theorem and short coherence times; learning must occur online.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the end-to-end process from orbital sensing to ground inference, comparing performance across different data aggregation architectures (Isolated, Centralized, Federated).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the EntangledEdge architecture (quantum data plane + classical control plane), compares its performance against various baselines (e.g., classical transmission, centralized learning), and validates scalability and robustness.
why_interesting: It addresses the practical challenge of integrating quantum sensing measurements into real-world, distributed machine learning pipelines, which is crucial for quantum networking and remote quantum computation.
